text: Port agent-intercom (Rust) to a feature-complete, CGO-free Go implementation. Authoritative spec: docs/decisions/2026-07-06-go-port-reference-brief.md. Deliberations: docs/decisions/2026-09-03-intercom-go-architecture-reconciliation-deliberation.md (Group A) and docs/decisions/2026-09-03-intercom-go-port-continuation-deliberation.md (roadmap + MCP decision). HARVESTED SO FAR: P0 foundation = 001-F/001-S (SHIPPED, merge 87b800d5d3a6457d86fecd12fb7a299f170af718); P1 error taxonomy + path containment = 002-F/002-S (SHIPPED, merge 9efb156, closure docs/closure/002-S-002-F-post-merge-closure.md); P2 config package = 003-F/003-S (HARVESTED 2026-09-03, queued). SUCCESSOR ORDERING - strictly sequential, one shipment per phase, no parallel implementation worktrees (P-016). P2 config and P3 credentials are tracked in stash 037B1552 and depend on 002-F. This entry now covers P4 onward: [P4 depends P3] internal/models plus SQLite risk slice via modernc.org/sqlite - 7-table schema and session_repo; models is IN P4 not P5 because session_repo.rs:8-11 imports models::{progress,session}; [P5 depends P4] remaining 7 repos plus retention; [P6 depends P5] ACP subprocess risk slice - spawner, handshake, codec, reader, writer, PLUS a consumer-side Notifier interface because acp/reader.rs:48 imports slack::client and would otherwise invert P6/P8; [P7 depends P6] AgentDriver interface, ACP driver, event consumer; [P8 depends P7] Slack Socket Mode risk slice, implements Notifier; [P9 depends P8] Slack surface - slash commands, modals, 9 handlers, US17 thread @-mention replies; [P10 depends P9] diff apply, approval workflow, terminal-command gate, policy, audit; [P11 depends P10] internal/agenttools - the RETAINED MCP HTTP tool endpoint with the 9 wire tool names check_clearance, check_diff, auto_check, transmit, broadcast, reboot, switch_freq, standby, ping; [P12 depends P11] resilience - stall detect/nudge/escalate, at-least-once steering, reconnect/repost, crash respawn+resume; [P13 depends P12] IPC plus intercom-ctl; [P14 depends P13] parity sweep across the 56/22/46/6 corpus plus the Playwright suite; [P15 depends P14] cutover decision, Rust remains fallback until parity. MCP DECISION (D1): retired as a SERVER MODE (no internal/mode, no McpDriver, no --mode/--transport, no stdio transport) but the HTTP TOOL ENDPOINT IS RETAINED at P11 - src/main.rs:365-372 shows start_sse has no mode guard and ACP subprocesses depend on it for HITL. Only the state<->slack import cycle must be broken in Go; driver/ is NOT in the cycle, and retiring McpDriver removes the sole driver->state edge. ORACLE CORRECTION 2026-09-03: references\\herdr is NOT the oracle - it is ogulcancelik/herdr, a Rust terminal multiplexer (0 hits for acp, AgentDriver, clearance, socketmode, ServerMode, stall_alert). It is plausibly relevant to stash A92E3FA0 (multiplexer) instead, and is left untouched and git-excluded. The AUTHORITATIVE ORACLE is softwaresalt/agent-intercom at C:\\Source\\GitHub\\intercom, commit 41df772, read-only and out-of-tree, verified by remote URL, module map, 21762 src LOC, and exact 56/22/46/6 corpus counts. NO BLOCKERS REMAIN.

Copilot Remote Multiplexer backend: per-workspace Go process with Bubble Tea TUI, gorilla/websocket server, Microsoft Dev Tunnels transport, coder/acp-go-sdk, in-memory State Hydrator for late-joiner iOS clients, and autoharness process/port orchestration. Source: docs/design-docs/intercom-go-backend-architecture.md. BLOCKED - requires architecture reconciliation before planning. Deliberation: docs/decisions/2026-09-03-intercom-go-architecture-reconciliation-deliberation.md (Group B). Three load-bearing conflicts with the agent-intercom Go port brief: (1) durability model - the brief's recover_state/ADR-0011, crash respawn+resume, at-least-once steering with origin_session_id rebind, and retention pruning are semantics unimplementable on an in-memory SessionState, while late-joiner hydration is definitionally in-memory; (2) operator surface is embedded in the persistence schema - slack_ts appears in 5 of 7 tables and thread_ts/channel_id are session columns, so Slack is not a pluggable presentation layer; (3) lifecycle ownership - one server routing many [[workspace]] channels under max_concurrent_sessions with intercom-ctl over IPC, versus one process per workspace with ports allocated by a Python parent. ARCHITECTURE REVIEW CORRECTION: the deliberation's unresolved option (c) mischaracterized AgentDriver as a seam for an additional operator surface. AgentDriver is AGENT-facing (SendPrompt/Interrupt/ResolveClearance). The multiplexer's TUI/WebSocket/iOS adapters are OPERATOR-facing. Composition would need a separate OperatorGateway interface over shared session events, with the SDK-backed ACP broker implementing AgentDriver. Reconciliation must still independently decide persistence model and deployment topology - AgentDriver does not resolve those.

intercom-go P3 successor: credential resolution (residual scope of the original config+errors slice). HARVEST HISTORY: [P1] error taxonomy + workspace path containment -> 002-F / 002-S (SHIPPED, merge 9efb156). [P2] config package -> 003-F / shipment 003-S (HARVESTED 2026-09-03, queued, 19 items: 1 feature + 5 sub-epics + 13 units). Plan: docs/plans/2026-09-03-intercom-go-p2-config-plan.md (review PASS, attempt 2). Deliberation: docs/decisions/2026-09-03-intercom-go-p2-config-deliberation-addendum.md. REMAINING SCOPE - [P3 credentials, depends on 003-F]: the 4-step credential precedence, the keychain provider, and a redacting Secret type. Oracle-grounded P3 contract: precedence is KEYCHAIN-FIRST within a mode-scoped chain - acp keychain, then *_ACP env, then shared keychain, then shared env - NOT env-with-keychain-fallback; keychain service constant is agent-intercom with the acp variant agent-intercom-acp and env suffix _ACP; app_token and bot_token are required, team_id is OPTIONAL and never fails (defaults to empty); authorized_user_ids comes from SLACK_MEMBER_IDS and IS required non-empty. The oracle has NO Secret<T> type - SlackConfig carries a hand-written Debug impl that redacts app_token and bot_token but leaves team_id AND channel_id visible; the Go redacting Secret type is an IMPROVEMENT, not a port, so its API is unconstrained by the oracle. Oracle test corpus to port: 8 credential tests. BINDING P2 BOUNDARY DECISION (plan Decision R7): internal/config is a PERMANENTLY secret-free file-schema package. P3 MUST NOT add app_token/bot_token/team_id/authorized_user_ids to config.Config - all four are #[serde(skip)] in the oracle and are never read from config.toml. P3 must return a separate ResolvedCredentials value composed with *config.Config in a higher-level bootstrap package; attaching secrets to config.Config would invert the dependency because credential resolution already consumes config. P2 CORRECTIONS THAT SUPERSEDE THIS ENTRY - the previously recorded 16 non-zero defaults is WRONG, it is 17 (slack_detail_level = Standard was missed); the 9 validation rules figure is a total across three oracle functions of which only 5 ran on the normal load path, unified to 10 hard rules in the Go port after mode retirement. The previously recorded OPEN QUESTION about the channel_id uniqueness check is RESOLVED (P2-D6): the oracle does not validate on hot-reload, but it DOES enforce uniqueness at ACP session start (src/slack/commands.rs:731), so the Go port enforces it eagerly at load and the divergence is recorded as V4. ORACLE: softwaresalt/agent-intercom at C:\Source\GitHub\intercom, commit 41df772, re-verified 2026-09-03 by HEAD and remote URL, read-only and out-of-tree, never modified. references\herdr is unrelated and untouched. NO BLOCKERS REMAIN for P3.

Add a machine-checkable oracle-drift gate: a script (plus CI wiring) that reads the pinned oracle commit from docs/oracle-pin.md, runs 'git -C <oracle-path> rev-parse HEAD', and fails when it does not match 41df772. Deferred from the 002-S plan review as residual P2 finding ARCH-5: the oracle is out-of-tree so the pin is currently DOCUMENTARY ONLY, which is the weakest link for future dark-factory (unattended) execution of phases P2-P14 - a drifted oracle would silently freeze contracts against the wrong revision with no detection. Kept out of shipment 002-S to avoid expanding a leaf slice with a new script and CI surface. Depends on 002.003.001-ST (docs/oracle-pin.md must exist first). Alternative worth evaluating: vendor the oracle's test fixtures into this repo so parity tests are self-contained and oracle-independent at runtime. Source: docs/plans/2026-09-03-intercom-go-apperr-pathsafe-plan.md, Plan Review residual findings.

DEFERRED SCOPE EXPANSION: internal/pathsafe has several Go-idiom P3 advisories from review: (1) splitPath is a redundant one-line wrapper around filepathSplitList; consider inlining or using strings.Split(p, string(filepath.Separator)) instead of hand-rolled indexing. (2) internal/apperr.Kind has no Stringer implementation, so bare %v/%d logging of a Kind prints an opaque integer rather than its name (Constitution Principle VI/Observability nicety). (3) apperr.kindSentinel has no bounds validation and no test asserting len(allKinds) tracks the exported Err* sentinel count, risking silent taxonomy drift if extended later. Out of scope per P-021 C1: none of these are required by the reviewed plan's acceptance criteria; all are style/robustness advisories. Source refs: feature 002-F, shipment 002-S. PR: (assign at PR creation). Review thread: N/A (pre-PR local review finding). Requires deliberation: no. Kind: task. Priority: low.

DEFERRED SCOPE EXPANSION: internal/pathsafe.hasPathPrefix builds prefix+separator which becomes a doubled separator when root.path is exactly the filesystem root (e.g. '/'), causing Resolve to incorrectly reject a valid resolution in that narrow configuration. Also, internal/pathsafe.NewRoot does not verify its canonicalized target is actually a directory (pointing the root at a regular file succeeds silently). Also, the GO-14 documented behavior (a dangling/broken symlink at the final path component is treated as non-existent via os.Stat) has no dedicated regression test locking it in. Out of scope per P-021 C1: none are required by the reviewed plan's acceptance criteria; all are narrow edge cases with no known real deployment impact for this primitives-only, zero-importer slice. Source refs: feature 002-F, shipment 002-S. PR: (assign at PR creation). Review thread: N/A (pre-PR local review finding). Requires deliberation: no. Kind: task. Priority: low.

DEFERRED SCOPE EXPANSION: internal/apperr.Newf's format string is not checked by go vet's printf analyzer (documented, finding GO-11), and .golangci.yml has no linters.settings.govet.settings.printf.funcs entry registering Newf as a printf-like function, so format-string bugs at future Newf call sites (projected ~470 AppError construction sites across later phases) are silently unchecked by the quality gates.
